title: Adoption cases linked to alleged Indonesian baby trafficking ring
asked: Ms Sylvia Lim asked how many approved adoptions are being reviewed further, how MSF is ensuring affected families get clarity and resolution quickly, and whether interim assistance is being considered, particularly where adoptees have not obtained Singapore citizenship.
response: Mr Goh Pei Ming said Indonesian authorities are investigating the alleged trafficking of Indonesian babies and Singapore is working with them, but MSF cannot comment on how many cases are under review. He said MSF is engaging affected families and working to review cases expeditiously while safeguarding the children's welfare. He explained that adoption and citizenship are separate processes, that citizenship is not automatic after an adoption order and can take up to 12 months, and that adoptive parents needing financial assistance may approach MSF for a case-by-case assessment.

key_points.point: Indonesian authorities are investigating the alleged trafficking of Indonesian babies, and Singapore is working with Indonesian counterparts.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Investigations by the Indonesian authorities into the alleged trafficking of Indonesian babies are underway.

key_points.point: MSF is engaging affected families to provide information on processes and address their concerns.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: MSF has been engaging affected families to provide more information on processes and to address their concerns as information becomes available.

key_points.point: MSF is working with authorities to review cases expeditiously while safeguarding the children's welfare and best interests.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: We are also working closely with the relevant authorities to ensure that cases are reviewed expeditiously, while safeguarding the welfare and best interests of the children involved.

key_points.point: No timeline for the investigations can be given at this point.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: We are unable to comment on a timeline at this juncture.

key_points.point: Adoption and citizenship processes are kept separate because they are governed by different legal frameworks and policy considerations.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: we keep the adoption process and the citizenship process separate because they are governed by different legal frameworks and policy considerations.

key_points.point: Granting of citizenship is not automatic following an adoption order.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: the granting of citizenship is not automatic following the adoption order

key_points.point: Prospective adoptive parents are informed that the citizenship process can take up to 12 months.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: We also inform them that the citizenship process can take up to 12 months.

key_points.point: Adoptive parents needing financial assistance may approach MSF, which will assess each case based on the circumstances.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: If the adoptive parents do need financial assistance, they may approach MSF and we will assess every case based on the circumstances.

key_points.point: The onus is on adoptive parents to ensure children are identified, matched and placed in accordance with the laws of Singapore and the child's origin country.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: the onus is on adoptive parents to try their best and ensure that children are identified, matched and placed in accordance with the prevailing laws of both Singapore as well as the child's origin country.

key_points.point: Agencies that knowingly bring in children of unknown and suspicious origin will be taken to task.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: If we do uncover that agencies are aware that the children they are bringing in are of unknown and suspicious origin and despite so, bring them in, they will be taken to task.

left_open: The number of approved adoptions being reviewed further
A timeline for when the review will be completed
Whether interim assistance will be provided specifically where adoptees have not obtained Singapore citizenship
supplementary: Timeline for the review, whether agencies could have detected suspicious circumstances earlier, and childcare costs while citizenship is on hold.

_dropped.point: MSF cannot comment on the number of cases currently under review.
_dropped.quote: MSF is unable to comment on the number of cases currently under review at this stage.
